reason: E1 shows mixed intergranular fracture at 700°C but does not provide compositional evidence for GB segregation of Ni, Cr, Mn. E2 shows improved ductility in a dual-phase alloy with Cr-rich precipitates and attributes it to absorption of embrittling elements, but the specific segregating species and direct GB cohesion measurements are not shown. Thus, the segregation mechanism is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
premises: At 600–700°C, single-phase CrMnFeCoNi HEA exhibits intergranular brittle fracture.
This embrittlement is caused by nanosegregation of Ni, Cr, and Mn to grain boundaries.
Preexisting Cr-rich precipitates can absorb these embrittling elements.
Absorbing embrittling elements into precipitates preserves grain boundary cohesion and ductility.
